newsitem.title: USA: CBOT May delivery market focused on wheat, oats.
newsitem.headline: CBOT May delivery market focused on wheat, oats.

text.p: Heavier-than-expected delivery notices posted on the May wheat contract was the key "surprise" noted by traders early Wednesday, first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT May agriculture futures contracts.
"Deliveries were pretty much what they were looking for but wheat deliveries were a little heavy," a trader said.

The market was expecting a heavy wheat delivery tally of up to two million bushels but the total posted Wednesday was 3.120 million bushels. That scenario could limit gains Wednesday in the nearby May contract, the traders said.
Produce Grain put out 2.450 million bushels of wheat.
There were no oat delivery notices posted which should be supportive to oat futures since some market sources were expecting up to two million bushels to be posted for delivery.
Soybean delivery notices posted at 500,000 bushels were within expectations of up to one million bushels, and heavy soyoil notices at 4,987 lots also were expected as were zero soymeal notices.
Corn delivery notices at 415,000 bushels will garner mild bearish attention because the market was not expecting any corn to be posted for delivery.
